thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: High kv-cache amplification detected for continuous-batching pipeline. p99 latency spike > 1.2s for hosted/text/generate (us-west-2). Affected model: Llama-v2-MQA. Trigger: sudden prefix cardinality increase. Escalation level: P1.

maria: paging, I'm on it. seeing sustained contbatch queue growth on mqa-serving nodes.

devon: can you dump contbatch metrics? queue length, avg batch size, kv hit ratio?

maria: past 10m: queue_len per-shard increased 4x, avg_batch_size dropped from 32->8, kv_hit_ratio down 78%->41%. attaching sample logs.

maria: ```
[2026-03-15T18:40:02Z] shard=shard-7 queue_len=312 inflight=8 avg_batch=9 kv_hits=41% 
[2026-03-15T18:40:22Z] shard=shard-7 queue_len=328 inflight=9 avg_batch=7 kv_hits=39% 
[2026-03-15T18:40:42Z] shard=shard-4 queue_len=298 inflight=6 avg_batch=8 kv_hits=42%
```

kevin: looks like a prefix-cardinality storm. probably new traffic pattern from a customer deploying massive prompt templates. if kv hit ratio collapses, contbatch degenerates -> huge queue and per-token CPU.

sophie: @maria which models are hitting this? is it all Llama variants or only MQA?

maria: mostly Llama-v2-MQA and a handful of Llama-v1 instances. Mistral + Qwen not affected yet.

oncall-bot: @engineering oncall assigned -> @devon. Please confirm mitigation plan and whether to page SRE.

devon: I can take oncall. immediate plan: 1) throttle contbatch batching windows on affected pools 2) enable prefix-KV eviction policy more aggressively 3) roll small canary of a batching config change to reduce queueing.

kevin: agree. quick CLI to shrink max_batch_window and enable faster kv-evict:

kevin: ```bash
redwoodctl patch pool --name=llama-mqa-usw2 --set=contbatch.max_window_ms=8 --set=kv.eviction.aggressiveness=high
```

maria: running the command on one pool now (shard-4/7). will watch queue.

maria: applied to shard-4. queue_len dropping slowly, avg_batch_size up to 12. p99 latency improving by ~200ms.

devon: start canary rollout to 10% of request capacity across 3 AZs. Expose rollout ID so we can rollback fast.

sophie: launching canary: `rollout create --config=mb-reduce-window-v1 --pct=10 --tag=contbatch-hotfix-237654`

incident-bot: ROLLOUT: canary started (id=contbatch-hotfix-237654). Monitoring 60m.

engineering-manager: customer impact? which apps/users hit errors/timeouts? any billing-adjusted customers?

maria: impacted customers: two mid-market customers (ids: cust-981, cust-1002) reported elevated latency and 10-20% increase in response-timeouts in the past 15m. No 5xx spike yet. Most traffic is slower but still succeeding.

kevin: set a temporary routing policy to shift high-qps traffic off the affected pool to dedicated fallback (costly but lowers customer impact).

devon: routing applied: `route set --from=hosted-usw2-llama-mqa --to=hosted-usw2-llama-mqa-fallback --pct=30`

maria: after routing bump, p99 for the main pool dropped to 420ms, and fallbacks are handling ~28% of requests. customers with strict SLAs see improvement.

sophie: canary metrics look good after 12m: queue_len stable, avg_batch_size 14, kv_hit_ratio creeping back up to 56%. no error increase. recommending expand to 50% in 10m.

devon: hold expansion at 50%. alert if p99 > 700ms or server cpu > 75% for 5m.

incident-bot: ALERT rule `contbatch-llama-p99` still firing on two shards intermittently; automation suppressed noisy repeats.

maria: ran quick postmortem notes: root cause likely a change in customer prompt templates that increased unique prefixes (high cardinality) causing cache dilution and reduced batch reuse. combined with contbatch config tuned for high kv_hit_ratio, we weren't resilient to loss of hit ratio.

kevin: followups: 1) add dynamic batching window that adapts by kv_hit_ratio 2) add prefetched prefix fingerprints to keep cold-start warm 3) alerting tuning to include kv_hit_ratio drops (not just latency).

engineering-manager: can we commit a temporary config toggle that automatically reduces batching window when kv_hit_ratio < 50%? need PR and owner.

devon: I'll own the PR for the toggle and a short-term alert tweak. aim to land in next 48h.

maria: customer comms: ops to reach out to cust-981 & cust-1002 with summary + mitigation steps. assign to @sophie for comms.

sophie: I'll draft the message: timeframe, observed impact, actions taken, next steps. copy legal and support.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in progress. canary healthy. routing applied. severity downgraded to P2 for tracking.

maria: quick ops checklist for post-incident:
- confirm expanded rollout to 50% and then 100% if stable
- monitor kv_hit_ratio and batch metrics 2h post-rollout
- capture debug traces for 3 representative requests from cust-981
- file follow-up RFC for adaptive batching

devon: expanding canary to 50% now. if stable, will hit 100% in 30m.

maria: thanks team. continuing to watch. will post a final update when fully rolled out. :thumbsup:

engineering-manager: great response. please schedule a blameless postmortem with timeline and action owners. date by EOD tomorrow.

maria: noted. closing on-call handoff to @devon.

devon: taking handoff. will monitor for 2h, then transfer to oncall rotation.

incident-bot: THREAD CLOSED FOR NOW: next update expected in 30m or on change.
